title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck is working with a localizer W on (Cat), the weak equivalences of categories, and its localization γ: Cat → Hot(W) = W^{-1}Cat. On the previous page he observed that the naive quotient Cat → \overline{Cat} (functors modulo the equivalence relation generated by elementary homotopies) does not preserve infinite coproducts. His counterexample: points f_n, g_n of the infinite zigzag Y = I_∞ (→←→←…) that are joined only by zigzags of homotopies of increasing length. He then conjectured that infinite sums do exist in Hot(W) and that γ preserves them.

On this page he reformulates the conjecture. For a family (X_j)_{j∈J} in Cat with X = ∐X_j, and any Y, the conjecture says the restriction map Hom_Hot(γX, γY) → ∏_j Hom_Hot(γX_j, γY) is bijective for every Y.

He then tries to prove this with a calculus of fractions. In it, a map X ⇢ Y of Hot is represented by a functor X → Y' together with a weak equivalence Y → Y' (fractions 'on the target side'). He notes that, with this description, neither injectivity nor surjectivity is clear, and he finds this 'bien gênant'.

a) Surjectivity. Given arbitrary φ_j: X_j ⇢ Y, each is represented by f_j: X_j → Y'_j with Y → Y'_j in W. Here Y'_j depends on j. The problem is to find one weak equivalence Y → Y' through which all the φ_j can be represented simultaneously. He invokes 'la théorie des pro-objets': the relevant index categories are filtering, so a common Y' exists for every finite subfamily.

The next page completes this step. He takes the amalgamated sum under Y of the Y'_j for each finite J_0 ⊂ J, then the filtered colimit over J_0. This requires W to be stable under such pushouts (along open/closed immersions) and under filtered colimits; this is the content of a Lemma. That gives surjectivity.

Injectivity is then reduced to showing: if f, g: ∐X_j → Y' satisfy γ(f_j) = γ(g_j) for all j, then γ(f) = γ(g). He warns that f_j ∼ g_j for all j does not imply f ∼ g (homotopy classes, as on the previous page), and that some 'Kan' hypothesis on a replacement Y' would be needed.

Purpose: establishing the basic exactness properties of Hot(W) (existence and preservation of sums) needed for the homotopy theory of Cat / modelizers being developed in parallel with Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs.
errors: No outright error. The worry is ultimately unfounded. For basic (fundamental) localizers, W is stable under arbitrary coproducts; for the usual Thomason equivalences the nerve preserves coproducts. Ho(Cat) ≃ Ho(sSet), and the localization functor Cat → Hot(W) preserves arbitrary sums: coproducts preserve weak equivalences and the coproduct is a homotopy coproduct. So the bijectivity holds, although his calculus-of-fractions route is not the efficient proof.

The pro-object/filtered-colimit argument tacitly assumes stability of W under pushouts along immersions and under filtered colimits. He only states this as a lemma on the next page, without proof here. The existence of a calculus of fractions of the stated form on Cat is itself not established on this page.

ideas.what: The localization Cat → Hot(W) should preserve arbitrary coproducts even though the homotopy-class quotient \overline{Cat} does not.
ideas.modern_name: Stability of (basic) localizers under coproducts; homotopy coproducts in Ho(Cat)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cisinski (Le localisateur fondamental minimal, 2004; Les préfaisceaux comme modèles..., 2006); Maltsiniotis (La théorie de l'homotopie de Grothendieck, 2005); for Thomason equivalences, essentially Thomason 1980
ideas.where_published: Themes of this kind appear in Pursuing Stacks / Les Dérivateurs; not sure this exact discussion appears there.

ideas.what: Gluing infinitely many fraction representatives X_j → Y'_j ← Y into one Y → Y' via finite amalgamated sums plus a filtered colimit (pro-object / filtering argument).
ideas.modern_name: Cofinality/filtered colimit argument; stability of weak equivalences under pushouts along cofibrations and filtered colimits
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard model-category technique (Quillen; Gabriel–Zisman for calculus of fractions)

ideas.what: Warning that objectwise homotopy (f_j ∼ g_j for all j) does not imply homotopy on the infinite sum, so a Kan-type fibrancy condition on a replacement Y' is needed.
ideas.modern_name: Need for fibrant replacement when computing homotopy classes; non-preservation of coproducts by naive homotopy categories

deep.surprise_reason: A working check of a foundational, now well-known property (Cat → Hot(W) preserves sums), using a clumsy calculus-of-fractions approach. The result is in the literature (Cisinski, Maltsiniotis), and the techniques are standard.
transcription_corrections: The crossed-out symbols in 'Hom_Hot([..](X), [..](Y))' look like a functor symbol (probably γ) applied to X and Y; Hot appears as a subscript under both Hom's.

'Il ne paraît que pour [-deux-] familles' is more plausibly 'Il se pourrait que pour des familles infinies [?] des sections (φ_j)…, il n'existe pas de (Y→Y')∈W commun pour toutes les φ_j, telles que X_j ⇢ Y se représente par X_j → Y''. That is, he is raising the possibility of failure, and the phrase 'commun pour toutes les φ_j' is underlined.
'A priori, on aura Y → Y'_j (commun. famille d'un ensemble)' is more likely 'Y → Y'_j (dépendant de j)'.

'elle ne serait certainement jamais' is uncertain; possibly 'elles me semblent probablement fausses, pour les mêmes raisons' (referring back to the previous page). 'Il n'est pas clair' / 'gênant !' reading is fine.
The top-right note 'Correspondance avec notations' is uncertain; the second word may be a name rather than 'notations'.
